summary: New box Part. Pass.: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (Jan 2.13/3326)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: Bas, Abuna, i dawmaṯe d kəmarnolox, ʕal u darbo laltaḥ, bu ṭuro wa, kətwo l ḥḏora kefe. Hawxa mḥawatto wa. Man d fatwo, maṣərwo fasto biya.
data.translation: Jan: But, Father, the tree I am telling you about was on the road below, on the mountain; there were stones around it. It was enclosed like that. Whoever passed would tie a rag on it.

rationale: First Detransitive Part. Pass. example; the whole short tree-and-stones context supplies the affected subject and enclosure before the state predicate. Supplied project machine translation [MT], not an edition translation.

The tree is the affected subject, surrounded by stones, and feminine mḥawatto wa expresses a resultant/static enclosure. One clear attestation supplies the Detransitive corresponding to active umzingeln; no military restriction is imposed.

data.turoyo: Mḥawaṭṭe u=maṭʕam, hani hbiṭi, maʕlalle iḏayye,
data.translation: Als sie das Speisehaus umstellten, wurden jene von Schrecken gepackt und hoben die Hände hoch.

rationale: Thin Preterit sense-1 cell; the complete consequence clause makes the encirclement and surrender understandable without surrounding narrative.

summary: All three occurrences illustrate II.1 umzingeln. Buildings and people can be encircled; this participant difference requires no new sense.

At 87/129 an overt l-marked pronominal agent precedes the encircled building. The next verse repeats the same encirclement event and supplies the other group’s fear and raised hands; it is a better context, not evidence for a second lexical use.
The unprefixed Infectum at 89/110 has a detective-group agent and a suffixed plural patient. The source writes mḥawtənne while the inherited quotation writes mḥawṭən-ne; keep this variation visible.
No supplied occurrence supports or challenges inherited sense 2, gern haben/gern kaufen wollen. Leave that existing sense and its example unchanged.

Round 2 only. Jan Beṯ-Şawoce English is project machine translation [MT]; readings rest on the supplied Turoyo. Existing and round-1 wording and numbering are retained. No edition translation is inferred.
The source writes mḥawatto with tt; the inherited root and active paradigm use ṭ. Preserve the Jan form instead of silently normalizing it.
The separate wa is a past copula with the feminine predicate; no active Preterit L-agent or invented finite Detransitive pair is inferred.
The nearby rag-tying custom explains the setting but establishes no new verb sense or fixed ḥwṭ idiom. Inherited active sense 2 remains as before.
Check the source t versus inherited ṭ in 89/110 against the edition or recording before treating the spelling as dialectal de-emphasis or correcting the inherited text.

Confirm mḥawatto as the feminine Detransitive Part. Pass. of ḥwṭ II and whether tt reflects assimilation/de-emphasis or transcription. Does the enclosure describe the stones’ arrangement rather than a fence?
Jan examples have project machine translations [MT], not edition translations. Editors should check these English renderings against the Turoyo before treating them as vetted translations.
Static enclosure by stones around a tree extends the participant domain beyond people and buildings without changing the core surrounding relation.
